newsitem.title: Bosnia: Bosnian disabled veterans block major road.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian disabled veterans block major road.

text.p: Disabled veterans of the mainly-Moslem Bosnian army and families of soldiers killed in action on Tuesday blocked roads leading into the central town of Kakanj, demanding unpaid pensions.

"I am leaving here only after I get my money. Until then the road remains blocked," said a one-legged man sitting on a log blocking the main Sarajevo-Kakanj road. His crutches were propped against the tree trunk.
Hundreds of automobiles were stranded by the felled logs.
Disabled war veterans are due approximately 80 DM ($52) monthly pension, like the families of soldiers killed in action.
Organiszers of the protest said all roads into the town and the main Kakanj-Zenica road were also blocked.
They ignored a representative of the town authorities who begged them to lift the blockade, saying their pensions would be paid on Wednesday.
"Nothing doing, pay them out now," one veteran said.
Journalists trying to check U.N. reports that a Croat Roman Catholic nun had been stabbed to death in Kakanj on Monday night was also denied permission to pass into town.
A spokesman for the International Police Task Force in postwar Bosnia, Andrea Angeli, said the the 46-year-old nun was stabbed six times.
He said the nun belonged to the Order of the Daughters of God's Love and was a native of Vitez, in a Croat-controlled pocket of central Bosnia some 20 km (12 miles) west of Kakanj.
